name: Shelomi
overview: Shelomi was a male member of the tribe of Asher, noted in Scripture primarily as the father of Ahihud. His mention is brief and focused on his role within his family lineage. No additional personal details or roles are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shelomi means 'at peace' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name given to him without direct divine attribution. This meaning may indicate a peaceful character or context, though the text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Shelomi is explicitly identified as a descendant of Asher and is recorded as the father of Ahihud. Beyond these relationships, Scripture does not provide additional family details for him.
scriptureSignificance: Shelomi's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as a patriarch within the tribe of Asher, specifically as the father of Ahihud. His mention helps establish genealogical and tribal connections important for understanding the organization and inheritance within Israel. Though briefly noted, his lineage contributes to the broader framework of God's covenant people.
